coachingPoints: Move your feet before your hands — slides beat reaches every time
Trace the ball with your lead hand to force the dribbler to protect it
Keep your chest facing the ball handler's chest to stay square
Force the ball toward your help — know whether your team wants middle or baseline denied
Never cross your feet while sliding; push with the back foot and step with the lead foot
Contest every shot without fouling — a clean contest beats a block attempt most possessions
commonMistakes: Reaching for steals instead of sliding the feet — one reach beats you off the dribble
Opening the hips and getting turned — stay square to the ball handler
Letting the ball handler go middle when your team is icing to the baseline
Fouling jump shooters by jumping into their landing space — contest with the body under control
description: Guard the ball handler one-on-one: stance, slides, angles, and how to contain the drive without fouling.
gameSituations: An isolation possession against your matchup
After a switch puts you on the ball
When your man catches the ball in the half court
Late clock when the offense tries to create off the dribble

howTo.detail: Start in a low defensive stance, one arm's length plus a half-step of space from the ball handler. Being too close invites a blow-by; too far invites a rhythm jumper.
howTo.title: Set up in stance at proper distance

howTo.detail: Watch the ball handler's midsection, not the ball. Keep your chest square to theirs so you can react to either hand.
howTo.title: Square up and lock in on the chest

howTo.detail: Slide laterally with drop steps and push steps, never crossing your feet. The back foot pushes, the lead foot steps, keeping the base wide.
howTo.title: Slide with the dribble, don't reach

howTo.detail: Hold your lead hand — the one on the ball side — at ball height to trace the dribble. Keep the other hand slightly behind to play the drive shoulder.
howTo.title: Trace the ball with your lead hand

howTo.detail: Use your slides to guide the ball handler toward your team's help: deny the middle if your scheme funnels baseline, or vice versa. This is called dictating direction.
howTo.title: Dictate the drive direction

howTo.detail: When the shot goes up, stay down, raise the high hand straight up to contest, and avoid leaning into the shooter. Then turn and find your man to box out.
howTo.title: Contest the shot, then box out

title: On-Ball Defense
whatIsIt: On-ball defense is guarding the player who has the basketball. Your job is simple to describe and hard to execute: stay between your man and the basket, keep him in front of you, and contest everything without fouling.

Good on-ball defense is mostly positioning and patience. You do not need to steal the ball or block the shot to win the possession. If the ball handler cannot get past you, cannot get a clean look, and is forced to pass with the clock winding down, you have done your job.
whyItMatters: Everything in team defense starts with the ball. If one defender cannot contain the ball, the whole defense has to rotate, which creates open shots everywhere else. Strong on-ball defenders reduce the need for help, which means fewer rotations and fewer breakdowns for the entire team.
